title: MPC minutes November 2026: written statement
text: My recent votes to increase Bank Rate by 25 basis points represented a ‘down payment’ to lean against second-round effects, reinforce credibility, and uphold ‘good policy’ (in the language of my Great Moderation speech). The challenge: projected CPI inflation reaches 4.9% by mid-2027 and would be some 25 basis points higher absent the measures announced at the latest Budget. This projection is conditioned on a significant decline in energy prices; similar futures curves earlier this year have not eventuated. My policy strategy importantly is informed by research, which points to non-linear inflation risks. Households are particularly attentive to energy and food price inflation, which may be reflected in 2027 wage demands. With CPI inflation at 3.5% in September, the economy has crossed the estimated statistical threshold into a high inflation-tight labour market regime where the asymmetric behavioural responses of households and firms support more robust second-round effects. A different research approach estimates that the economy may well have breached the policy credibility threshold, which worsens the policy trade-off. Moreover, a substantial inflation risk premium is in the UK yield curve, reflecting five years of above-target inflation, where it has averaged 4.7%. Therefore, from a risk management and credibility perspective, a 50-basis point hike in Bank Rate is ‘good policy’.
